items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear, but the intent is buried in magic values with no comment explaining them: `setStateOptions?.meta === 'restore'` toggles `#restoredFromPersister`, and an undocumented `consumed?: boolean` field sits on the public PersisterRestoreResult.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The marker lives in query.ts, not a dedicated persister.ts. A hidden `#restoredFromPersister` flag is reset across setData/reset. The Vue useBaseQuery adapter was changed even though adapters should need none. `Partial<QueryState<any, TError>>` uses any on a public signature.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The persisted state is cast straight through (`result.state as Partial<QueryState<TData, TError>>`) with no visible check or cleanup of counters, timestamps or status. A string sentinel `meta === 'restore'` drives the restore logic. Hidden tests pass.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: The helper is exported and uses a symbol brand (`Symbol.for(...)`, which is global and so forgeable). The restore seems to route through setState with meta 'restore' rather than a dedicated reducer action. Success callbacks are not called and fetchStatus ends idle (tested). Whether bulk restore shares the same path can't be confirmed from the diff.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: New exports are additive and tests pass, but the QueryPersister type in types.ts was edited. Vue useBaseQuery gained an extra `else { unsubscribe = observer.subscribe(...) }`, which changes how existing adapters behave when not restoring.
